## 3.12 Host attachment planning

The typical FC host attachment to the Storwize V7OOO is done through SAN fabric. However, the system allows direct attachment connectivity between its 8 Gb or 16 Gb Fibre Channel ports and host ports. No configuration is required for host systems that are this configuration. However, the maximum number of directly attached hosts is severely limited by the number of FC ports on Storwize V7OOO's nodes. special using

The Storwize V7OOO imposes no particular limit on the distance between the Storwize V70OO nodes and host servers. However, for host attachment; the Storwize V7OOO supports up to three ISL hops in the fabric. This capacity means that the server to the Storwize V7OOO can be separated by up to five FC links; four of which can be 10 km long (6.2 miles) if long wave Small Form-factor Pluggables (SFPs) are used.

Figure 3-9 shows an example of a supported configuration with Storwize V7OOO nodes using shortwave SFPs

Figure 3-9 Example of host connectivity

<!-- image -->

In Figure 3-9, the optical distance between Storwize V7OOO Node 1 and Host 2 is slightly over 40 km (24.85 miles) .

To avoid latencies that lead to degraded performance; avoid ISL hops whenever possible. In an optimal setup; the servers connect to the same SAN switch as the Storwize V7OOO nodes.

Note: Before attaching host systems to Storwize V7OOO; review the Configuration Limits and Restrictions for the IBM System Storage Storwize V7OOO at this IBM Support web page.
